title: Cursor Rules: How to Write .cursorrules and .mdc Files That Actually Work
summary: Learn how to write Cursor rules that make your AI agent project-aware. Covers .cursor/rules/*.mdc format, four activation modes, glob patterns, and 10 real examples.
body_markdown: Write a rule when the pattern is repeatable and predictable — the signal is correcting the AI for the same mistake three or more times. One-off mistakes (misunderstanding a specific function, wrong variable name in a particular context) are better handled inline. Cursor's guidance: "Start simple. Add rules only when you notice Agent making the same mistake repeatedly." Over-engineered rule sets become maintenance overhead; focused ones stay useful for months. For how this same discipline applies to the broader agentic coding workflow, see our[what is Claude Code](https://blink.new/blog/what-is-claude-code) primer.
